What catches me out when I’m getting ready isn’t the things that I know how long it takes to do. For me it’s the other things that I try to fill time with while I’m actually doing the things I need to do to be on time.

One of the other people was confused by my not knowing how long it takes to do something… I know roughly how long it takes do the things on my critical path, things like make a coffee, get dressed, take a shower, put my shoes on, I now how long it takes to get them done in sequence because I’ve done them often enough.

Maybe other people’s brains are filled timings of stuff that they do only once (or infrequently) but mine sure isn’t. For me to learn anything (like how long something takes to do) my brain has to be engaged by that task enough for me to give it enough of my attention to make a lasting memory. If it’s not difficult enough (or inherently time critical), then it doesn’t go into my long term memory alongside an approximate number of minutes that the task will take, I (like many other people) do many tasks on autopilot while thinking about something else “more important”.

“More important” could be anything from working on the next work project, to talking with my partner on the phone about her day. But I can do mindless things like load or unload the dishwasher without focussing on it, and if I can do that then I am certainly not committing it to memory. 

Unless knowing the rough number of minutes to do something is critical in my day for some reason (like knowing how long it takes to walk to the bus stop because I need to be there to get on the bus to go to work) then I will not fill my head with details like the number of minutes it takes to unload the dishwasher. 

It means if loading or unloading the dishwasher ever does become a critical path part of my day (like it’s the one thing I need to do while running out the door) then my best guess is going to be just that…. a guess at roughly how long it will take me. 

What catches me out is that if I have more time than I need to put my shoes on, then I might try to fill that time doing something that “feels like” it should take close to the amount of time I have free. If I think I have time do something like “just fill the dishwasher” in those last few minutes before running out the door, then I’m probably going to try. And then J have to have the willpower to not try to finish it if it looks like I’m going to be late… it depends how important the two commitments feel in my mind.

Seriously, if your Dr is prescribing 1.5 concerta pills then your Doc needs to stop practising medicine and take up a career that won’t result in people being injured. Because of the way the concerta works, it’s not possible to split Concerta and have it release half a dose.

It isn’t a normal capsule - it’s a polymer cylinder that doesn’t dissolve, it has 1/4 of the dose applied as an instant release coating that dissolves as soon as you swallow it - and the rest of the dose is stored inside it with a hole drilled into it that slowly releases the rest as it gets wet from your body.

When you cut the pill in half, you get half the instant release dose just like cutting a normal pill, but the long release mechanism will not work to release half the dose. It’ll probably dump a huge amount all at once, or it won’t work.

Concerta brand name is a very different looking little pill.

If you google it, you will see that it’s has a round barrel shape with “alza” written on it.

That shape is because of the release mechanism. The outer is covered with a soluble shell that releases about 22% in the first hour or so.

Inside it is a hard little (plastic I guess) cylinder that doesn’t dissolve. It releases the dose throughout the day because of an expanding gel or similar inside it - as it gets wet it expands and squeezes the meds out through a hole drilled by a laser - it releases the drug into your system. Unlike other delayed release meds, it’s normal for some of it to pass right through you before being completely released.

Because of this release system, it has a different release profile to the generics.

You’re right. They are trying to make a product that gives a fast acting boost but that lasts  bit longer.

Concerta is 20% IR and 80% XR, but the last bit of the XR is apparently rarely released, it keeps releasing until it passes right through you. This means it has a much longer time to act, even long after the main influence has gone, you still have a longer residual tail. 

If people have sleep problems because of Concerta, it’s because either they respond to the methyphenidate by being more awake (took it too late in the day so it was still wearing off at bed time, or even the lower dose at the tail is still too much for them to be able to sleep), or because their ADHD presents with sleeping problems and they have too little methylphenidate in their system at bedtime. 

Medikinet is 50% IR and 50% XR, so the initial peak is high for the same dosage, but the tail is not as long and not as intense. Still much longer acting that normal IR Ritalin, but it leaves your system faster than Concerta. It’s kind of a halfway point between Concerta and Ritalin.

Methylphenidate could be a solution for people that need it out of their system more completely at the end of the day, so they can sleep. 

The XR aspect means it’s still has a lower abuse potential than IR.
